nodes.question: What complementary analysis was adopted alongside the FSE method in the study?
nodes.answer: The Gini mean analysis was adopted as a complementary analysis to the FSE method.
nodes.paragraph: In this study, we argue that GI adoption and implementation success hinge on effectively conveying the multifunctional prospects and a keen consideration of client objectives. These gaps were examined in the con- text of a developing nation through a combination of stationary attribute analysis and fuzzy evaluations. Researchers have adopted fuzzy synthetic evaluation method to draw inference in subjective constructs (Zafar et al., 2022). Further, FSE method was also adopted in the built environment to examine the drivers of circular economy in modular integrated construction (Wuni et al., 2022). However, FSE applications in GI knowledge assessment have not been explored, particularly in the developing nation context. To ensure a holistic conveyance of GI benefits and attributes, the Gini mean analysis was adopted as a complementary analysis to FSE to peruse the pivots among built environ- ment professionals in GI projects. Gini index as a stationary measure of dispersion, pro- vides an arbitrary factor that is central to pioneering a concept (GI). A combination of geometric mean analysis, Gini coefficient, principal factor analy - sis and fuzzy synthetic evaluations was adopted in this study to provide an in-depth understanding of the multifunctional drivers of GI among built environment profession- als in developing regions.

nodes.question: What are the key outcomes expected from the research on energy consumption in the Sichuan Plateau?
nodes.answer: The key outcomes include identifying high energy consumption factors and proposing energy-saving improvement measures along with an economic suitability analysis.
nodes.paragraph: As a unique geographical unit in China, the Sichuan Plateau can exchange and share its research and practical experience in energy efficiency improvement with similar regions in the world. Methodology and material As shown in Fig. 1, the research method mainly uses field measurements, questionnaire surveys, and energy simulations to conduct an in-depth analysis of the factors affecting the energy consumption of residential buildings in Sichuan Plateau, and to measure and quantitatively analyse the indoor thermal environment of local traditional residential buildings. The key factors of high energy consumption are identified, and some energy- saving improvement and optimization measures and economic suitability analysis are proposed. Research object The Sichuan Plateau region is composed of three prefectures: Garze Prefecture, Aba Prefecture, and Liangshan Prefecture, as shown in Fig. 2, Aba is located in the Sichuan Plateau region, about 104.27 least longitude, 30.35 latitude, the highest altitude in the territory is about 6250 m, and the average altitude is 3500 4000 m. According to the Code for Thermal Design of Civil Buildings, there are five climatic zones in China, namely severe cold areas, cold regions, hot summer and cold winter regions, mild regions, and hot summer and warm winter regions30.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What gap in analysis does the paper aim to address regarding energy subsidy cost-recovery?
nodes.answer: The paper aims to address the gap of considering the trade-off between distributional impacts and efficiency in energy subsidy cost-recovery analyses.
nodes.paragraph: Farrell ( 2021 ) nds losses in consumer surplus equivalent to between 6-18% of domestic consumption value due to British tariff deviationsfrom the Coasian structure. Similar effects were observed in the US natural gas industry. Davisand Muehlegger ( 2010 nd that volumetric prices are signi cantly higher than marginal cost, resulting in an estimated US$2.7 billion welfare loss per annum. Borenstein ( 2012 ) nds that US natural gas prices are approximately 30% higher than marginal cost, resulting in a con-siderable consumer welfare loss. The welfare loss associated with water utility pricing hasbeen analysed in a similar way (e.g., Crew and Kleindorfer 1976 ; Swallow and Marin 1988 ; Renzetti 1992 ). Porcher ( 2014 ) nds that French water customers face prices on average 8% greater than marginal costs, resulting in a welfare loss of approximately e8 million. This paper identi es the optimal surcharge design given the relative importance of equity and ef ciency. Analyses relating to energy subsidy cost-recovery have focussed on distri-butional impacts and have failed to consider the trade-off with ef ciency. This paper is the rst to provide this contribution.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: According to the findings, which type of economic variables has greater explanatory power for CO2 emissions in Spain?
nodes.answer: Selected economic variables have greater explanatory power than the common economic factors extracted using the 2SKF procedure.
nodes.paragraph: In this paper, we analyse the short-run relationship between economic activity and CO 2emissions in Spain, by tting a SADFM to annual rates of growth of Spanish CO 2 emissions with the factors extracted by 2SKF from a large set of Spanish macroeco-nomic variables. 2SKF is an unsupervised factor extraction procedure, which combinesinformation contained in all macroeconomic variables independently from the target variable. Additionally, we also consider factor extraction orientated towards pre- diction of the rate of growth of CO 2emissions. In particular, we extract factors using partial least squares (PLS) as proposed by Wold ( 1966 ). We conclude that the explana- tory power of selected economic variables is larger than that of common economic factors when the latter are extracted using the 2SKF procedure. However, the pre-dictive power of the common factors increases when they are extracted using PLS. We nd that the PLS common factors recover some explanatory power for explaining CO 2emissions beyond the information content of the selected individual economic indicators. Our results somehow differ from those found by Bennedsen et al. ( 2021 ) for the US economy as the outstanding predictors for CO 2emissions in Spain are private consumption and maritime transport of merchandise, while theirs rely more on IP .

nodes.question: What does the analysis conducted by Bennedsen et al. (2021) indicate about the explanatory power of the factors once certain variables are included?
nodes.answer: The analysis indicates that once selected explanatory variables, particularly Industrial Production (IP), are included in the model, the explanatory power of the factors is negligible.
nodes.paragraph: Furthermore, using the nonlinear factor-augmentedregression proposed by Bai and Ng ( 2008 ), he concludes that the polynomial terms of the factors are not signi cant and, therefore, the EKC is not found in the short run. More recently, Bennedsen et al. ( 2021 ) propose a structural augmented dynamic factor model (SADFM) for annual CO 2emissions in the US. As in Fosten ( 2019 ), the economic activity is represented by common factors, which are extracted from a large set of annual macroeconomic US variables using the two-step Kalman Iter (2SKF) procedure of Doz et al. ( 2011 ) instead of PC. The SADFM also includes additional explanatory variables selected from the same set of economic variables byusing procedures based on Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) of Tibshirani ( 1996 ), Elastic Nets (EN) of Zou and Hastie ( 2005 ) and Autometrics of Doornik ( 2009 ) and Doornik and Hendry ( 2009 ). They conclude that, once the selected explanatory variables, in particular, Industrial Production (IP), are included in the model, the explanatory power of the factors is negligible.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Economic viability of energy-efficient appliances_qna_007
nodes.label: Methodology
nodes.question: Which econometric techniques does the empirical study utilize to infer consistent outcomes?
nodes.answer: The study utilizes unit root analysis, bounds testing, the Johansen cointegration approach, the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) model, dynamic OLS, and variance decomposition.
nodes.paragraph: A few studies, including Warsame et al.32, on the renewable energy-environmental degradation nexus in Somalia have failed to consider trade openness. The country depends heavily on the export of agricultural and livestock products, and most consumed goods are imported. In addition, to infer consistent outcomes, this empirical study uses various econometric techniques, including unit root analysis, bounds testing, the Johansen cointegration approach, the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) model, dynamic OLS, and variance decomposition. Finally, the findings can inform evidence-based policies that align economic progress with environmental protection, thus charting a course towards a more sustainable future for Somalia. The remainder of this paper is structured as follows. The second section reviews related theoretical and empirical literature. In the third section, the methodology details the research approach, data collection, and analytical methods. The fourth section presents the results and discusses outcomes. Finally, the study concludes with relevant policy suggestions. Theoretical and empirical literature Theoretically, the literature relies on the pollution haven hypothesis PHH and the factor endowment hypothesis FEH to explain the association between trade openness and the environment8,36.
